questions.q: A hill is $500m$ high. Supplies are to be sent across the hill using a canon that can hurl packets at a speed of $125m{s}^{- 1}$ over the hill. The cannon is located at a distance of $800m$ from the foot of the hill and can be moved on the ground at a speed of $2m{s}^{- 1}$ so that its distance from the hill can be adjusted. What is the shortest time (in seconds) in which a packet can reach on the ground across the hill? (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Given, height of the hill (h) = 500 m

u = 125 m/s

To cross the hill, the vertical component of the velocity should be sufficient to cross such height.

$∴$ ${\text{u}}_{\text{y}} ≥ \sqrt{2 \text{gh}}$

$≥ \sqrt{2 × 1 0 × 5 0 0}$

$≥ 1 0 0 \text{m/s}$

But ${\text{u}}^{2} = {\text{u}}_{\text{x}}^{2} + {\text{u}}_{\text{y}}^{2}$

$∴$ Horizontal component of initial velocity

${\text{u}}_{\text{x}} = \sqrt{{\text{u}}^{2} - {\text{u}}_{\text{y}}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{{\left(1 2 5\right)}^{2} - {\left(1 0 0\right)}^{2}}$

$= 7 5 \text{m} / \text{s}$

Time taken to reach the top of the hill

$\text{t} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \text{h}}{\text{g}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 × 5 0 0}{1 0}} = 1 0 \text{s}$

Time taken to reach the ground from the top of the hill t' = t = 10 s

Horizontal distance travelled in 10 s

$\text{x} = {\text{u}}_{\text{x}} × \text{t}$

$= 7 5 × 1 0$

$= 7 5 0 \text{m}$

$∴$ Distance through which canon has to be moved

= 800 - 750

= 50 m

Speed with which canon can move = 2 m/s

$∴$ Time taken by canon $= \dfrac{5 0}{2}$

${\text{t}}^{″} = 2 5 \text{s}$

$∴$ Total time taken by a packet to reach on the ground

$= {\text{t}}^{″} + \text{t} + {\text{t}}^{′}$

$= 2 5 + 1 0 + 1 0$

$= 4 5 \text{s}$ .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is projected on a frictionless inclined plane of inclination $37 °$ at an angle of projection $45 °$ from the inclined plane as shown in the figure. If after the first collision from the plane, the particle returns to its point of projection, then what is the value of the reciprocal of the coefficient of restitution between the particle and the plane?
questions.solution:
While going upward the time of flight is

$T = \dfrac{2usin \alpha}{gcos \beta}$

So the range on the inclined plane is

$R = \left(ucos \alpha\right)T - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(gsin \beta\right){T}^{2}$

Just after the collision of the projectile with the inclined plane, the components of its velocity down the inclined plane and perpendicular to the inclined plane are

${v}_{∥} = \left(gsin \beta\right)T - ucos \alpha$, ${v}_{⊥} = eusin \alpha$

The time of flight while going down the inclined plane is

${T}^{'} = \dfrac{2eusin \alpha}{gcos \beta} = eT$

The range of the projectile while going down is

$R = \left[\left(gsin \beta\right)T - ucos \alpha\right]eT + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(gsin \beta\right){e}^{2}{T}^{2}$

$⇒ \left[\left(gsin \beta\right)T - ucos \alpha\right]eT + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(gsin \beta\right){e}^{2}{T}^{2} = \left(ucos \alpha\right)T - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(gsin \beta\right){T}^{2}$

$⇒ ucos \alpha\left(1 + e\right) = \left(gsin \beta\right)T\left[\dfrac{1}{2} + e + \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{2}\right]$

Substituting the value as $T = \dfrac{2usin \alpha}{gcos \beta}$ we get

$⇒ cot \alpha\left(1 + e\right) = 2tan \beta\left[\dfrac{1}{2} + e + \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{2}\right]$

$⇒ 3{e}^{2} + 2e - 1 = 0$

$⇒ e = \dfrac{1}{3}$ or $\dfrac{1}{e} = 3$
